Sparse log-concave NMF with automatic best rank tuning

Source: vignettes/articles/log-concave-nmf.Rmd
log-concave-nmf.Rmd

A GC–MS chromatogram can contain several compounds at the same retention time. The time course of a compound is its elution profile, and the relative signals it produces across ions form its mass spectrum. Each measured scan contains a mixture of those contributions.

A fixed convolution model places the same local response shape at each candidate position. That works well when the peaks have similar shapes. Broad, tailed or overloaded peaks can require several adjacent spikes to approximate one compound. logconNMF() begins with such a dictionary and then estimates a separate log-concave profile and spectrum for every retained component. This lets the model combine compatible fragments and refine both the peak shapes and the spectra.

The factorization

For n ordered scans and m channels, write the mean as

M = H S + B A + O,\qquad H\in\mathbb{R}_+^{n\times K},\quad S\in\mathbb{R}_+^{K\times m}.

Here K is the number of components, BA is an optional smooth background and O is a known additive offset. Component k contributes the outer product of column k of H and row k of S. The positive support of a profile is contiguous. On an evenly spaced grid, log-concavity means 2\log H_{ik}\geq \log H_{i-1,k}+\log H_{i+1,k} within that support. This includes familiar Gaussian and exponentially tailed peak shapes.

Each column of H sums to one. The corresponding row of S then contains integrated channel intensities and can be normalized to a spectrum of relative intensities. The fit compares likelihood and rank so that another profile must explain enough of the signal to justify its inclusion.

Fit profiles, loadings and background

The signal below contains six co-eluting components. Rows index ordered scans; columns index mass channels. The formulation also applies to other ordered multichannel measurements.

library(L0glm)
library(logconNMF)
data(gcmsData1)
Y <- gcmsData1
X <- convMatrix(convKernel("gaussian", 65L, list(sigma=8)), nrow(Y))
B <- matrix(1, nrow(Y), 1L)
fit <- logconNMF(Y, X=X, background=B,
  family=quasipoisson("identity"), precluster=8L, correlation="auto", ncores=8L)
fit$rank
dim(fit$H)
dim(coef(fit))
GIC(fit)

The constant background is supplied as a single column of ones. Use PSF estimation to build X when the initial response shape is unknown or varies with position.

Inspect the recovered components 

matplot(as.matrix(fit$H), type="l", lty=1, xlab="Scan", ylab="Profile")
matplot(t(coef(fit)), type="h", lty=1, xlab="Channel", ylab="Loading")
L0glm::plotMat(t(fitted(fit)), xlab="Scan", ylab="Channel")
patterns <- coef(fit) / rowSums(coef(fit))
fitted_signal <- fitted(fit)
fit$seconds
Background-corrected ion traces, six resolved log-concave profiles and a 2 by 3 panel of recovered spectra

All 670 channels are retained, and factors are returned in increasing profile-apex order. The upper panel uses a square-root display to retain weak grey ion traces; the six spectra use base-peak relative intensities. The GCMSprime tutorial develops the chromatographic interpretation, file input and reports.

A broad asymmetric component

The beer-volatile window combines narrow overlapping peaks with a much broader acid contribution. A low-dimensional spline accounts for the smooth background:

data(gcmsData2)
Y2 <- gcmsData2
t2 <- as.numeric(rownames(Y2))
X2 <- convMatrix(convKernel("gaussian", 65L, list(sigma=6)), nrow(Y2))
B2 <- splines::bs(t2, df=4L, intercept=TRUE)
fit2 <- logconNMF(Y2, X=X2, background=B2,
  family=quasipoisson("identity"), precluster=32L, correlation="auto", ncores=8L)
fit2$rank
fit2$contained_fusion$broad
Log-concave profiles and full-channel spectra, including the broad component

The table reports one direct fit of each matrix with eight OpenMP threads and one BLAS thread on an Intel Core i9-11950H. Constructing the PSF dictionary and background basis is outside the timing.

Window Scans Channels Components Quasi-GIC Seconds
Hydrocarbon window 119 670 6 247,888 7.96
Beer volatiles 1,764 518 38 1,467,426 67.00

The GCMSprime tutorial times the complete CDF-to-MSP workflow separately and provides diagnostic plots and downloadable spectra.

Automatic best rank tuning

The initialization keeps a permissive pool of components while native constrained likelihood updates refine their profiles and spectra. Final rank selection applies the requested temporal information adjustment. Small fragments contained within a broad profile are compared with an equally refined unmerged local model on all original channels.

The default lambda="gic" compares complete fits by likelihood and component count. After dividing the likelihood by the original channel count, each retained component incurs one rank charge. On the unscaled likelihood the charge is m\lambda_{\mathrm{IC}}, with an optional temporal information adjustment. Profile complexity and background coefficients have no extra rank penalty.

fit$objective
fit$history[, c("stage", "delta", "accepted", "compounds")]
fit$cleanup
fit$initialization
fit$contained_fusion
c(AIC=AIC(fit), BIC=BIC(fit), GIC=GIC(fit))

Reported criteria count mK, where K is the fitted rank, plus estimated shared noise parameters. Other presets are "aic", "bic", "ebic" and "mbic". A nonnegative numeric lambda supplies the penalty per selection degree of freedom. Each retained component incurs m\lambda before temporal adjustment. The rank objective gives the full convention.

Choose a noise model

All seven models use identity-link nonnegative means and the original observation scale. Gaussian measurements can have negative errors around that mean.

Model R specification Variance at mean \mu
Gaussian gaussian("identity") \phi
Poisson poisson("identity") \mu
Quasipoisson quasipoisson("identity") \phi\mu
NB2 mgcv::nb(link="identity") \mu+\mu^2/\theta
NB1 nb1(dispersion=2, link="identity") \phi\mu
Censored Gamma gammaCensored(dispersion=.2, link="identity") \phi\mu^2 before censoring
Common-scale Gamma gammaScale(scale=2, link="identity") \sigma\mu before censoring

Here \phi denotes the dispersion and \sigma the common Gamma scale. Positive dispersion or theta arguments fix the parameter. Omitted shared parameters are estimated from temporal differences. A negative NB2 theta initializes at its absolute value and enables likelihood-improving updates. Quasipoisson uses a scaled Poisson kernel and corresponding quasi-criteria.

Zero Gamma intensities represent left censoring at a detection limit, set by control=list(censor=0.5); their contribution is the probability below that limit. See the noise models for scores and parameterizations.

Faster initialization and smooth backgrounds

precluster=32L initializes in at most 32 size-adjusted outcome groups, then returns to every original channel. precluster=FALSE uses the full matrix directly. control$linkage selects Ward Poisson or Bregman grouping. The original channel count sets the rank charge in both workflows; final scoring uses the original observations and specified noise model.

For a longer signal, replace the constant background with a low-dimensional nonnegative spline basis:

B <- splines::bs(seq_len(nrow(Y)), df=4L, intercept=TRUE)

Background coefficients are fitted conditionally on the component signal and remain unpenalized in rank selection. Known additive signals use offset; weights can be shared across channels or channel-specific.

The default correlation="auto" estimates a lag-one working information adjustment. "none" uses independent-observation rank charges; a supplied nonnegative correlation fixes the adjustment. Marginal noise variance stays in the likelihood. The mathematical article develops local solvers, hard shape constraints, aggregation and complete pseudocode. Continue with simultaneous multisample NMF for shared loadings and sample-specific profiles.
